Linde plc operates as an industrial gas company in the United States, China, Germany, the United Kingdom, Australia, Mexico, Brazil, and internationally. It offers atmospheric gases, including oxygen, nitrogen, argon, and rare gases; and process gases, such as hydrogen, helium, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, electronic gases, specialty gases, acetylene, etc. The company also designs and constructs turnkey process plants for third-party customers, as well as for the gas businesses in various locations consist of air separation, hydrogen, synthesis, olefin, and natural gas plants. It serves a range of industries comprising healthcare, chemicals and energy, manufacturing, metals and mining, food and beverage, and electronics. Linde plc was founded in 1879 and is based in Woking, the United Kingdom.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond (TLT) reversed to the downside on Thursday and has yet to exceed its March 3 closing high of $92.57. We thought the ETF was in a minor five-wave advance, with the next resistance just below $94. That is the location of the prior high on December 6 and is an important 61.8% retracement of the decline from mid-September 2024 until early January 2025. However, a failure from here would look more like a three-wave ABC advance, and suggests the possibility of a pullback. Key support for TLT is in the $90 region. The COT data is all over the place: bullish for the two-, and five-year Treasury, slightly bullish for the 10-year, and bearish for the 30-year. Seasonality has turned bearish this month and stays that way until the end of April. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) is trading at $68.25/barrel and is again attempting to bounce from the bottom of its multi-year trading range in the $64 to $66 region. In addition, WTI looks like it finally might break its downtrend and see some decent upside. That said, breaking below the $64 to $66 range could cause a very sharp move lower as there are probably sell stops right under this key support. On the upside, the bearish trendline off the peak since mid-January is just above $68, the declining 200-day average is at $71.50, and chart resistance sits in the mid- to high-$70s. The COT data has really caught our eye and has turned bullish. The last few times this occurred, WTI rallied $10 to $20/barrel. Seasonality is bullish and stays that way until September. (Mark Arbeter, CMT)
